key_insight: PrivMeSA lets a local clinical agent decide what to share with remote LLMs, using reinforcement learning and a reusable lesson memory to improve accuracy while sharply reducing patient-data exposure.
clinical_relevance: This could support safer hospital or emergency-department LLM workflows by preserving specialist help without repeatedly sending identifiable patient details off-device.
method: Local agent handles each patient encounter and selectively consults remote specialist LLMs.
Reinforcement learning balances clinical task accuracy against disclosure and re-identification risk across the full outbound transcript.
A local lesson memory distills completed cases into generalized guidance for reuse in later encounters.
evidence_signal: On an MIMIC-IV-ED-based benchmark, PrivMeSA improved mean task accuracy by up to 15.8 percentage points and reduced personal-detail disclosure from 98.0% to 0.2% of cases.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the privacy-risk model and the lesson memory, so real-world deployment would still need strong governance and validation across diverse clinical settings.
paper_title: PrivMeSA: Privacy-Aware Self-Evolving Multi-Agent System for Medicine via Local-Remote LLM Collaboration
